findings.claim: The 60,000 ms ceiling now exists as three independent values — PROMPT_REFINER_SHADOW_EVIDENCE_MAX_DURATION_MS (evidence core), PROMPT_REFINER_SHADOW_RUN_UNKNOWN_AFTER_MS (run contract, which unknownTelemetry writes verbatim as the sweep's durationMs), and a literal 60000 in the DB CHECK — with no assertion that the writer bound stays greater than or equal to the unknown-after interval.
findings.reproduction: Raise PROMPT_REFINER_SHADOW_RUN_UNKNOWN_AFTER_MS in lib/promptRefinerShadowRunContract.ts to 90_000 (and refresh the contract digest literal the module's self-check prints). unknownTelemetry() then emits durationMs 90_000, terminalInputIsValid refuses it, and every unknown sweep returns PROMPT_REFINER_SHADOW_TERMINAL_INVALID, so stale dispatch intents can never be closed. The DB integration sweep tests would surface this, so it is a latent coupling rather than a live defect; deriving the bound (or asserting PROMPT_REFINER_SHADOW_RUN_UNKNOWN_AFTER_MS <= PROMPT_REFINER_SHADOW_EVIDENCE_MAX_DURATION_MS in tests/promptRefinerShadowRunContract.test.mjs, and pinning the migration literal to the constant) would close it.

verdict.nextAction: Merge as the reviewed v4 implementation; optionally pin the three copies of the 60,000 ms ceiling to one derived constant in a later change.
